short: Lost America, absorbed Ireland, outlasted Napoleon, and reigned fifty-nine years.
full:
George III was the first Hanoverian born in Britain and reigned longer than any king before him. His early attempts to choose ministers freely produced a decade of unstable governments before Lord North settled matters, and it was under North that the American colonies were taxed, resisted and lost: the war ended with Yorktown in 1781 and independence was recognised at Paris in 1783.

William Pitt the Younger then gave the reign stability through the wars against revolutionary and Napoleonic France. The Irish rebellion of 1798 led to the Act of Union, which created the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland on 1 January 1801; the king's refusal to accept Catholic emancipation alongside it drove Pitt from office. George suffered recurrent episodes of mental illness, now often attributed to bipolar disorder, and after 1810 was permanently incapacitated. His son ruled as Prince Regent until the king died, blind and deaf, at Windsor in January 1820.
